patient.name: Emma Ross (index patient — one of 15 casualties)
patient.chiefComplaint: Multi-casualty school bus vs. passenger car collision — 15 patients on scene; this record follows the responding paramedic's first triaged patient

history.hpi: Second-arriving ALS unit responds to a school bus vs. sedan collision on a two-lane highway. The bus, carrying 22 students and a driver, rolled onto its side after impact; the sedan's single occupant is trapped. Approximately 15 patients have injuries ranging from minor to critical, scattered across the scene. This scenario follows the responding paramedic acting as triage officer, with Emma Ross (10F) as the first patient triaged using START.
history.events: Bus rolled after side-impact collision; Emma was thrown from her seat and struck the aisle, unable to bear weight on her right leg since the crash

scene.dispatch: Multi-vehicle collision with a school bus, multiple patients reported, highway location, mutual aid requested
scene.location: Two-lane rural highway; school bus on its side in the northbound lane, sedan against the guardrail 40 feet away
scene.safety: Fuel odor near the sedan, downed utility line 30 feet from the bus, bystanders attempting to self-extricate students — scene not yet fully secured
scene.bystanders: Bus driver ambulatory and assisting students; several parents arriving on scene and attempting to approach
visualCues: Bus on its side with students visible through emergency exit windows, ambulatory and non-ambulatory mixed
Approximately 15 patients spread across a 100-foot radius, varying severity
One patient (sedan driver) trapped, fire/rescue en route for extrication
Emma Ross seated against a guardrail, tearful, holding her right thigh, unable to stand
Bus driver performing informal head count and directing ambulatory students to a grassy area

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: The paramedic arrives second-due to a chaotic multi-casualty scene: a rolled school bus and a sedan, roughly 15 patients of mixed severity, incomplete scene safety, and no triage structure yet established.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Unable to bear weight on right leg; upper extremities and left leg intact
otherFindings: Right mid-thigh deformity and swelling, no open wound
Follows commands, oriented to self and place
Scene: multiple other patients visible at varying distances, none yet assessed
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "My leg hurts so bad, I can't stand up. Where's my brother?"

transitions.condition: The paramedic rapidly assesses scene safety and scope, then assigns roles and responsibilities among arriving EMS personnel before approaching individual patients.

phases.name: Scene assessed and roles assigned
phases.description: The paramedic functions as the senior clinician on scene: confirms scene safety concerns (fuel odor, downed line), requests the resources the incident actually needs, and assigns triage/treatment roles before beginning patient-by-patient sorting.
phases.triggerCondition: Recognizing the scene overwhelms immediately available resources, the paramedic takes command, addresses hazards, requests additional units, and assigns roles so that triage, treatment, and transport can proceed in parallel rather than one clinician working one patient at a time.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Unable to bear weight on right leg
otherFindings: Additional units en route per request
Triage, treatment, and transport roles verbally assigned to arriving crews
Downed utility line flagged and perimeter established

expectedActions.shortAction: Assign triage, treatment, and transport roles to arriving EMS personnel before patient contact
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Senior EMS clinician rapidly assesses scene and assigns roles and responsibilities to EMS personnel
expectedActions.rationale: Without designated roles, resources default to treating one patient at a time instead of sorting the whole scene first.

expectedActions.shortAction: Begin sorting all patients using START/JumpSTART before providing individual treatment
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Sort patients using a locally agreed upon MCI triage process which is the START/JUMP-START (Simple Triage and Rapid Transport)
expectedActions.rationale: Rapid sorting identifies which patients need immediate life-saving intervention before time is spent on any one patient.

transitions.condition: The paramedic applies the START Respiration-Perfusion-Mental-status algorithm to Emma: she is unable to walk (deformed leg), respirations are present and under 30/min, radial pulse is present, and she follows commands — categorizing her as Delayed rather than Immediate.

transitions.if: Full treatment given before sorting complete
transitions.condition: Instead of tagging Emma and moving to the next patient, the crew stops to fully splint and treat her before any other patient on scene has been triaged, delaying identification of patients in the Immediate category elsewhere on scene.

phases.name: Emma triaged using START
phases.description: Emma is categorized Delayed per START (cannot walk, but breathing without difficulty, has a palpable radial pulse, and follows commands). She receives a tag and a splint for her femur, and the paramedic moves on to continue sorting the remaining patients rather than staying with her.
phases.triggerCondition: START assessment (walk/breathe/perfuse/mental-status) places Emma in the Delayed category: she cannot walk due to the leg injury, but has no airway, breathing, or circulation compromise requiring immediate intervention.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right leg splinted; distal pulse, motor, sensation intact
otherFindings: Paramedic moving to next untriaged patient
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Thank you — please go help the others too."

expectedActions.shortAction: Tag Emma Delayed per START; do not remain with her — continue sorting remaining patients
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Triage categories are recommended and should be guided by local protocols: immediate, delayed, minimal, expectant, dead
expectedActions.rationale: Correct categorization prevents both under-triage (missing a critical patient) and over-triage (tying up resources on a stable one).

expectedActions.shortAction: Splint the right femur fracture in position found before moving to the next patient
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Splint obvious extremity fractures per the Extremity Trauma/External Hemorrhage Management Guideline
expectedActions.rationale: A brief splint limits further injury and pain without requiring the clinician to remain with a Delayed patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Re-triage Emma and all other tagged patients periodically for the duration of the incident
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Re-triage frequently for duration of MCI
expectedActions.rationale: Patient status can change; a Delayed patient can deteriorate to Immediate if not reassessed.

transitions.condition: Once all 15 patients are triaged and tagged, transport proceeds in priority order — Immediate patients first, then Delayed, with Minimal patients assessed for appropriate transport.

phases.name: Sorting complete, transport prioritized
phases.description: All patients have been triaged and tagged. Transport proceeds by category — Immediate patients transported first to trauma centers, Delayed patients (including Emma) second, Minimal patients assessed and transported appropriately, with continuous re-triage throughout.
phases.triggerCondition: With all patients sorted, the incident moves into the transport phase, prioritized strictly by triage category rather than order of arrival on scene.

otherFindings: All 15 patients tagged and accounted for
Immediate-category patients already en route to trauma centers
Emma awaiting transport as part of the Delayed group
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Is my brother okay? Can I go with him?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport Immediate-category patients first, then Delayed patients, then assess Minimal patients for transport
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: First transport immediate patients ... Second, transport delayed patients ... Assess minimal patients for appropriate transport decision
expectedActions.rationale: Strict category-based transport order gets the most critical patients to definitive care fastest given limited transport resources.

phases.name: Full treatment given before sorting complete
phases.description: By fully treating and staying with Emma — a Delayed patient — before the rest of the scene is sorted, the crew delays discovery of Immediate-category patients elsewhere, including a student with an evolving airway compromise who is not found and treated in time.
phases.triggerCondition: Time spent providing complete, unhurried care to one non-critical patient before the rest of the scene is triaged directly trades against the time-critical patients who have not yet been found.

otherFindings: Several minutes elapsed with only one patient triaged
Radio report from another crew: an unresponsive student found late with airway obstruction
Incident commander requesting status of triage progress
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Am I your only patient? What about everyone else?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Stop extended single-patient care; resume rapid START sorting of all remaining patients immediately
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Triage and transport most critical requiring immediate in-hospital care first
expectedActions.rationale: The MCI goal is the greatest good for the greatest number — time must be redirected to finding all Immediate patients, not perfecting care for one Delayed patient.
